Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The Aussie players are out in the middle. Eleanor Larosa to bowl first. Jemma Botha and Simone Lourens to open for South Africa. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

Right then, 106 is what South Africa Women Under-19 need to become the first finalists of the 2025 Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup. They have the batting prowess but have batted a total of about 26 overs in the whole tournament. Australia Women Under-19 have a stellar bowling attack and things could go down to the wire. Join us for the crucial run chase up next.

Ashleigh van Wyk, the star with the ball for South Africa Women Under-19 is down for a chat. Ashleigh van Wyk thinks that the team has played well and reckons it is their day. Adds that she didn't pick up wickets leading into this contest but gave it her all in this game and reckons that there was some spin in the track. Goes on to say that she tried to slow it up whereas Seshnie Naidu is generally a bit flatter. Adds than the whole of South Africa is behind them and they feel confident.

Australia Women Under-19 will be a tad bit disappointed with that batting effort but will also know that no one has scored 100 runs against them. After opting to bat first, they lost a wicket on the first ball and things became worse quite quickly. Just when Lucy Hamilton started to fire, she fell too and then it was a stand between Eleanor Larosa and Caoimhe Bray that steadied the ship. Larosa struggled in the middle but Bray did manage to score some vital runs and got into the 30s. After that it was Ella Briscoe who played a fine unbeaten cameo of 27 from 17 balls that actually got them over the three-figure mark.

After being asked to bowl first, South Africa Women Under-19 started in fine fashion as Nthabiseng Nini picked up a wicket off the first ball and then inflicted a run out as well before skipper Kayla Reyneke got the big wicket of Lucy Hamilton and made it 30/3 in the Powerplay. The spinners then came in and slowed the scoring rate without doing much damage. However, once they were able to break the fourth-wicket stand, things changed. There were a couple of wonderful catches and it was Ashleigh van Wyk who bowled in the second half of the innings and picked up four wickets to keep the Aussies down to a low score.

For the first time in this tournament, South Africa Women Under-19 bowled their full quota of 20 overs and they will feel they have done a fine job at that. They managed to pick up wickets throughout the innings barring one phase of play and have restricted Australia Women Under-19 to 105 runs which is slightly under-par.

A couple of runs to end! Kayla Reyneke fires it in full on leg, Ella Briscoe backs away and drills it back past the bowler down to long on and races back for the second run. The throw comes in at the keeper's end and the keeper just fails to knock the bails over. Australia Women Under-19 finish with 105/8 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to play! The umpires have taken their places in the middle and the players of South Africa Women Under-19 can be seen in a huddle before striding onto the field of play. It will be the duo of Grace Lyons and Ines McKeon to open the batting for Australia Women Under-19. Nthabiseng Nini has the new ball in hand and she is raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game but first, the young mascots bring out the flags of the respective nations and lineup alongside the two sets of players. The national anthems will now be played and it will be Australia's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of South Africa.

PITCH REPORT - Stacy-Ann King is pitchside. She says that overhead conditions are nice and blue and there's a nice breeze as well. Says that there have been nine matches played here and spinners have ruled the roost with the average first innings total being 107 and reckons there are cracks on the pitch but should play well.

South Africa Women Under-19 skipper, Kayla Reyneke says that they are pretty excited to get going and the vibes around the game are pretty nice. Adds that they have had a pretty good run so far and it is going to be tough not having played a full game but they are raring to go. Informs that they also have one change in their side.

Lucy Hamilton, the captain of Australia Women Under-19 says they will bat first as the pitch and conditions look good and they want to play their best cricket. Adds that they took a lot of positives from the last game and will look to turn things around here. Goes on to inform that they have one change in the side with Juliette Morton coming in for Kate Pelle.

Australia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Grace Lyons (WK), Ines McKeon, Lucy Hamilton (C), Caoimhe Bray, Eleanor Larosa, Hasrat Gill, Ella Briscoe, Chloe Ainsworth, Lily Bassingthwaighte, Tegan Williamson, Juliette Morton (In for Kate Pelle).

South Africa Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Jemma Botha, Simone Lourens, Fay Cowling, Kayla Reyneke (C), Karabo Meso (WK), Mieke van Voorst, Seshnie Naidu, Luyanda Nzuza (In for Diara Ramlakan), Ashleigh van Wyk, Monalisa Legodi, Nthabiseng Nini.
TOSS - Australia Women Under-19 win the toss and they will BAT first.

Right then, the stage is set for an exciting contest but as it has been the case throughout the competition the conditions will be overcast. However, the chances of rain playing spoilsport aren't much and hopefully, we should get a full game in. Who do you reckon will be the first finalists of the 2025 Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned as the toss and team sheets aren't far away.

Australia Women Under-19 on the other hand also had an unbeaten record but that was broken in their final Super Six game with a loss to Sri Lanka but the Aussies have played much more cricket in terms of overs and should be a bit more familiar with conditions as well. They do possess a lethal pace attack and have some big hitters up top but consistency will be key if they are to defeat the Proteas and seal a place in the final.

South Africa Women Under-19 are unbeaten in the competition so far but aren't the only unbeaten team and they haven't had a complete game of T20 cricket either given all the rain around but their bowling has been excellent, especially their spinners who might prove to be pivotal in this clash. However, their batting is untested and there might be a few nerves jangling for them in that department.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all. We are at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur for the first semifinal of the 2025 Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup where South Africa Women Under-19 will go up against Australia Women Under-19 for a spot in the grand finale and it's set up to be a fascinating clash.

Sixteen teams battled fiercely on the grand stage, and now only four remain in the race for the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025 title! The first semi-final promises an electrifying clash as South Africa Women Under-19 take on Australia Women Under-19 at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur. Australia, a dominant force throughout the tournament, cruised through the early stages unbeaten before suffering a shocking defeat against Sri Lanka in their previous game, a result that may have shaken their confidence ahead of this crucial encounter. While their batting vulnerabilities have surfaced in patches, their last outing was a nightmare they will be desperate to forget as they step into this high-pressure match with a renewed mindset. The Aussies boast an explosive opening duo in Kate Pelle and Ines McKeon, who have consistently provided strong starts, but their middle order has faltered more often than they would like. Skipper, Lucy Hamilton has been a key anchor in the batting unit, yet much more will be expected from the rest of the lineup, particularly against quality spin. On the bowling front, Hasrat Gill and Tegan Williamson have been among the wickets, but the entire attack will need to be at its sharpest if they are to regain control on this massive occasion. On the other hand, South Africa Women Under-19 have had a rather unusual journey to the semi-finals, having not played a single full 40-over game in the tournament so far. Either they have wrapped up matches too quickly against lower-ranked opponents, or rain has intervened to curtail their games, denying them valuable time in the middle. Their last group-stage fixture against the USA was washed out without a ball being bowled, leaving them short on match practice heading into this all-important clash. While this lack of game time could be a disadvantage in a high-stakes fixture, South Africa have shown immense promise in the limited opportunities they have had. The top order, led by Jemma Botha and Simone Lourens, has been among the runs, although their middle order remains relatively untested. With the ball, Kayla Reyneke has been a standout performer, alongside Monalisa Legodi, both of whom will have crucial roles to play in containing Australia’s batting firepower. While both teams bring their own strengths and weaknesses, making them evenly matched on paper, this semi-final is set to be an absolute thriller where nerves and composure will determine who punches their ticket to the grand finale.
